questions.question: Why do Express projects usually export the app from app.js and call listen() in a separate server.js?
options: Express 5 refuses to start if listen() is in the same file as routes
supertest needs the app object and starts it on a temporary port itself, so tests never bind a fixed port
It makes the app run faster in production
node:test can only import files that do not call listen()
questions.explanation: supertest takes the app, binds it to an ephemeral port for each request and closes it, so tests do not clash with a server on port 3000.

questions.question: A test calls request(app).get("/todos/1").expect(200) but forgets to await or return it. What happens?
options: The request is skipped and the test is marked as todo
The test can finish and pass before the request completes, so a failing assertion goes unnoticed
node:test automatically waits for all pending HTTP requests
questions.explanation: The supertest chain is thenable; without await or return the test function resolves immediately and the assertions run too late to fail it.

questions.question: Which supertest feature lets a test log in once and send the session cookie on later requests?
questions.explanation: An agent stores cookies from responses and sends them on subsequent requests, like a browser.

questions.question: Several test files share one MySQL test database and tests fail randomly when run with node --test. What is the most likely fix?
options: Mock the database in every test
Point the tests at the development database
Remove the beforeEach cleanup so data accumulates
Run with --test-concurrency=1 (or a database per worker) and reset data in beforeEach
questions.explanation: node --test runs files in parallel processes by default, so they interfere through shared tables. Serialise them or isolate databases, and reset state before each test.
